Two boaters. One dog. A helicopter crew ready to help. 🚁🐾

On October 6, Alaska Army National Guard aviators rescued two overdue boaters and their dog after their vessel became stuck in icy water north of the Arctic Circle.

The boaters had reached a nearby cabin. A Nome-based UH-60L Black Hawk crew flew to their location, about 75 miles east of Kotzebue, with two Nome Volunteer Fire Department EMTs aboard.

The crew spotted the group, landed in a clearing on the tundra and flew them to Kotzebue, where they were handed over to Alaska State Troopers.

That’s aviation doing good: bringing people, skills and a capable aircraft together to close a distance that would be difficult to cover on the ground.

And yes—the dog came along. 💛

Source: Alaska Department of Military & Veterans Affairs, October 7, 2026; National Guard report, October 8, 2026.
